Chapter 8: Managing Energy, Not Just Time.
As our ambitions grow and those to-do lists seem endless, the real challenge starts to shift. It’s not just about finding enough hours in the day anymore—it’s about managing our own energy.
Think about it: Time management by itself can only take us so far. Real productivity and a sense of fulfillment? That comes from understanding—and respecting—our natural rhythms of energy, focus, and motivation.
Managing your energy means tuning in to your physical, emotional, and mental well-being. It’s about noticing when you feel most awake, creative, or sharp, and then matching your most important tasks to those peak moments.
On the flip side, it’s also about giving yourself permission to rest and recharge when your energy dips, instead of forcing yourself to power through.
So, how do you actually put this into practice? Here are a few ideas:
First, pay attention to your daily patterns. When do you feel most energized? When do you feel drained?
Next, try scheduling your toughest or most demanding work during those high-energy windows. Save the routine or less important stuff for times when your energy naturally dips.
And don’t forget to build in regular breaks, a bit of movement, and moments that spark joy—these little things can help you recharge and keep going.
For example, maybe you’re someone whose creativity peaks in the morning, while the afternoon is better for catching up on emails or admin work. By shaping your day around these personal insights, you’ll likely find that you get more done—with less struggle and stress.
But there’s another side to this—emotional energy. The people you interact with, your environment, even your own inner dialogue, all play a role in either topping up or draining your energy reserves.
Practicing gratitude, connecting with others, or spending time on projects that matter to you can actually boost your motivation and resilience.
At the end of the day, managing energy is about working with your body and your mind, not against them. It’s a kinder approach—one that accepts you have limits and reminds you to find balance.
So, the key takeaway? When you focus on managing your energy—not just your time—you set yourself up for sustained performance and well-being, not just today, but for the long run.
